title: proof_coverage's label fallback reads a printed filesystem path as a tooth label, so a green seal that echoes a tool's verdict lines parses to a red tooth
intention: teeth_printed's third pattern (_MARKER_LABEL: an indented marker word then a label) does not take a label that is a filesystem path as a tooth, so dfe6's green seal reads zero red teeth, and a genuine indented red tooth still reads red.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on origin/main 2889bdd1f: test_NO_GREEN_SEAL_IN_THE_CORPUS_PARSES_TO_A_RED_TOOTH reds on exactly one of the corpus's green seals, cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_a_host_seam_seals_on_this_box_only.json, whose stdout_tail echoes the host-seam verifier's own lines ('         red  /tmp/dfe6-host-seam-scratch.../host-testing-dfe6c1432fc8.json on akiendelllinux', after 'ok test_a_red_verify_seals_red_and_is_not_proven'): data from a verify that is SUPPOSED to seal red, which the label fallback reads as a red tooth named by the path. ADJUDICATED against each side's why. The tooth's why is the invariant 'a proof that ran green must not have its own output read back as a failing tooth, because the reader would be manufacturing the red': it is right and stays unchanged. The seal's stdout is the tester's verify lines echoed so the teeth show what the child said: it should not have to dodge a parser, and the next proof that echoes a tool's verdict lines would repeat it. The parser's own why for the third pattern is 'a marker punctuated as a REPORT, not a sentence', and a path is no tooth label: the tooth's name is an identifier or a sentence, so the narrow fix is in the parser.
traces_to: Law 7 (a reader may not manufacture a red at a record of truth), Law 3.
how: In teeth_printed, a label match whose text begins with an absolute path (a '/' or '~' start, or a drive letter and a separator) is skipped (the line mints no tooth). Nothing else about the three patterns changes. New proof: three teeth. Red-first.

clauses.claim: teeth_printed over stdout holding the line '         red  /tmp/x/host.json on box' returns it in neither green nor red

teeth_printed over indented lines '  red  the backdate refusal' and '  ok   the backdate refusal wrote no slate' and a 'FAIL: a unified line' colon line still reads them (the narrow guard walls off nothing)
over the repo's real seals, no GREEN seal's stdout_tail parses to a red tooth (the invariant tooth in test_proof_coverage.py reads green)
teeth_printed over '  red  cairn/x.json on box' (a RELATIVE path echo) mints no tooth, and over '  red  a/b tests pass' (a slash and no file extension) still reads red

decisions.text: D1: the path guard in teeth_printed (a label starting like a path is not a tooth).
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; clause 3 reads the real seals the way test_proof_coverage.py's tooth does.

out: cairn/devices/tester (dfe6's proof and its seal stand as they are)

measured.saw: 1 of the corpus's green seals parses to a red tooth: cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_a_host_seam_seals_on_this_box_only.json -> ['/tmp/dfe6-host-seam-scratch.4026531836-481112-mw9s8so2/host-testing-dfe6c1432fc8.json on akiendelllinux']
measured.how: pc.teeth_printed over every green validation's stdout_tail on origin/main 2889bdd1f (the tooth's own loop)

measured.saw: plan v2 (CairnCommons 83d84e0b): an absolute-only guard still mints a tooth from a RELATIVE path echo ('  red  cairn/x.json on box'); clause 4 added, built at cd71722c2 (tooth 4 red against the absolute-only guard, green fixed)
